A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references; v2's Appendices A–G were also inspected.

before.justification: v1 reports original neural PDE-solving experiments on HJB, BSB, and Bender–Zhang problems, including accuracy, runtime, discretization, horizon, and floating-point results.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and adds batched-training results, dimensionality and runtime analyses, and a pendulum-control experiment.

M1.justification: The core Stratonovich/Heun integrator is retained, but v2 introduces batched training that separates forward rollout from backward-loss evaluation, subsamples trajectory points, and stops gradients through forward states (Algorithms 1 and 3). Appendix G.5 also adds a control-policy rollout adaptation with specified gradient blocking.

E1.justification: The original PDE benchmarks remain. Appendix G.6 adds nonlinear pendulum swing-up, extending evaluation to a first-order optimal-control problem with induced-policy cost assessment. Appendix G.3 also expands the represented HJB state dimensions to 2–500.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same five methods. However, EM-BSDE (NR), included in v1's Table 2 runtime comparison, is omitted from the corresponding v2 overhead comparison. Newly discussed methods such as Deep Runge–Kutta are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds training with 1024 subsampled rollout points, runtime-based accuracy comparisons, and pendulum cost/PDE-error evaluation. Its stated RL2 formula also changes the summation endpoint from N−1 to N. This documents a metric change without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds full-versus-batched comparisons, HJB dimensionality sensitivity, runtime analyses, and pendulum spatial-error maps. The floating-point study expands from BSB to HJB and BSB. The original discretization and skip-length analyses remain, with v1 Figure 4 becoming v2 Figure 5.

E5.justification: The three-initialization-seed accuracy reporting is retained, while v2 explicitly identifies Table 1's ± values as one standard deviation. Per-case runtime uncertainty disappears with the original timing breakdown. Neither version establishes an increase in run counts or introduces significance testing.

E6.justification: Original Table 1 accuracy values and BSB precision results are retained. v2 adds batched results, HJB precision results, dimensionality/runtime curves, and pendulum outcomes. Table 4 reports Heun PDE error 18.6, between EM-BSDE's 78.94 and FS-PINNs' 3.38. Original per-case absolute runtimes are removed; batched results reflect a different procedure.

T1.justification: v2 strengthens regularity assumptions, adds explicit global-loss theorems and proofs, revises some SDE-level remainders from O(τ) to O(√τ), and supplies a self-contained Heun convergence argument in Appendix F. Model-free/control derivations are also added. Some new formulas are inconsistent: the k-step normalization in Equations 3.7/4.8 conflicts with the full-horizon scaling used in Proposition E.4.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: one-step EM losses have persistent discretization bias, Heun removes that bias, and Heun restores competitive performance with PINNs. New implementation and experimental evidence do not materially redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix C specifies the information needed for model-free use, including trajectories and driving noise. Appendix G.5 explains why first-order control PDEs change which solver requires Hessians. v2 also adds an interpretation of differing HJB/BSB precision sensitivity and revises the computational-cost explanation around batching.

D1.justification: v2 adds rollout pseudocode, subsampling size, gradient-blocking instructions, explicit per-problem Stratonovich equations, and pendulum parameters. The network, optimizer, hardware, and code-access information are retained. Absolute timing details are removed, and Algorithms 1/3 introduce a terminal-loss sign inconsistency: (u+ϕ)² versus (u−ϕ)² in Algorithm 2 and the earlier description.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces v1's blanket statement about unstudied integration schemes with a distinction from prior Deep Runge–Kutta work on original BSDE losses. Appendix B substantially expands positioning relative to control variates, splitting, fully nonlinear solvers, tensor trains, and BSDE convergence theory, with corresponding added citations.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: detailed proofs move into Appendices D–F, benchmark definitions and precision analysis move into G, and the introduction's contribution list is removed. Background losses are presented through explicit horizon/step notation, and short-/long-horizon terminology becomes one-/multi-step terminology.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains separate full/batched blocks; Table 2 is redesigned as an aggregate overhead comparison; Table 3 expands and moves to the appendix. v2 adds Table 4, runtime/scalability/error-map figures, and algorithm boxes. Existing figures are retained and redistributed, including the renumbered skip-length plot.

improvement.justification: The new batched procedure materially addresses v1's computational bottleneck: Table 2 reports 2.03× PINNs overhead for batching versus 36.37× for full rollouts, with competitive accuracy in Table 1. Explicit assumptions and convergence arguments, scalability/control tests, and clearer applicability limits substantially strengthen the paper. New normalization and terminal-loss inconsistencies, plus lost timing detail, are drawbacks, but the practical and evidential gains remain substantial.
